newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: INSTANT VIEW - Draft of S.Korean financial reforms.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Draft of S.Korean financial reforms.

text.p: Following are analysts' immediate reaction to the 18-point draft of short-term financial reforms presented by South Korea's Presidential Commission for Financial Reform to President Kim Young-sam on Monday.
RHEE NAMUH, HEAD OF RESEARCH AT DONGBANG PEREGRINE SECURITIES:
"It has no substance. I do not expect dramatic changes in the financial industry this year."
"If the government does really want to restructure the industry it should give autonomy to financial institutions."
PARK KYUNG-SUH OF THE KOREA INSTITUTE OF FINANCE:

"The impact will be limited. But I believe financial reform means letting financial institutions do everything they want. The proposal has no impact of a 'big bang.' But it's meaningful that the commission paved a way for a reform.
"I believe 70 to 80 percent of the proposals will be implemented this year as the finance ministry does not need to oppose them, as most of them are what they have considered."
HWANG MIN, ECONOMIST OF SHINHAN RESEARCH INSTITUTE, AN AFFILIATE OF SHINHAN BANK:
"I cannot find anything suprising with the short-term proposals. I expect something more substantial from the longer-term proposals.
"In fact, our financial industry is not ready for free and hot competition. We need the government's firm vision and concrete blue print to reform the financial industry."
